key_insight: A target-value reconstruction corrects the inward-shift bias caused by one-sided spreading in diffuse-interface immersed boundary methods, improving boundary enforcement for compressible flow simulations.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate and efficient CFD of complex geometries with better no-slip and thermal boundary-condition handling without adding meaningful computational cost.
method: Analyze the one-sided spreading operator to estimate the effective boundary displacement.
Reconstruct target values so imposed conditions match the geometric boundary for Dirichlet and Neumann cases.
Embed the correction into the fully one-sided diffuse-interface immersed boundary method (FODIBM) coupled to a hybrid lattice Boltzmann solver.
evidence_signal: Across multiple grid resolutions and 2D/3D test cases, the improved method reduced L2 and L∞ errors, cut no-slip and isothermal boundary errors by 77% and 85%, and preserved roughly second-order convergence.
watch_item: The correction is localized to target-value evaluation, so performance may still depend on accurate boundary displacement estimation and careful implementation for new geometries.
paper_title: An improved fully one-sided diffuse-interface immersed boundary method with target-value reconstruction for compressible flows
